title: a cross-estate citation names a tracker that cannot be found from where it is written
body:
# 0020: a cross-estate citation names a tracker that cannot be found from where it is written

## Tags

provenance, commits, cross-estate, monikers, citations

## Summary

Three landed devbin commits -- 77aba5c, 7a232e4, 254f63e (2026-08-17, the project.referent work) -- cite "Issue 0049". Measured across all eight candidate repos on this machine, no tracker holds an issue 0049: Intent (a gap in their canon range, their node's derivation), devbin (range 0001..0016 at the time), Lamplight (high-water 0004), Baize (0001), Conflab (0008), and Laksa, Prolix, Riffle (no issue yet raised via `intent issues`; hv's framing 2026-08-24 -- the feature post-dates those projects, which is a date, not a convention choice). The last four were re-derived by lamplight-vc with the deriving command on record. Separately, 254f63e says "per vc" -- and monikers are estate-scoped, so with vc nodes now live in five projects the attribution is unresolvable from the commit alone. Even knowing the window's author (dc, the DevX Claude sessions, per hv 2026-08-24), the referents stay dark.

## Reproduction

`git log --oneline 77aba5c 7a232e4 254f63e` here, then `intent issues show 0049` in any of the eight repos. Also the recorded false lead: a bare-number grep across estates returns five confident hits at Laksa -- ST0049, a completed steel thread whose title sounds adjacent and whose content is unrelated (laksa-vc). Qualify by estate and tracker type, or do not grep.

## Root Cause

Cross-estate work carries citations written in the AUTHOR's frame: an issue number without its tracker, a moniker without its estate. Within one estate both are unambiguous; the moment work flows between estates (which the vendoring model makes routine), the citation's referent stays behind.

## Impact

Provenance archaeology that should be one command took four nodes, eight repo measurements, and an hv ruling on framing -- and still ends at "referent unfindable". The 0016 lesson one level up: a citation is a claim about a pointer, and these pointers name no address space.

## Proposed Fix

A commit-message convention, one line in usage-rules.md and a candidate for upstream Intent guidance: cross-estate references are qualified -- `<project>#NNNN` for issues (`intent#0054`, `devbin#0016`), `<project>/<node>` for monikers (`intent/vc`, not "vc"). Unqualified forms stay legal for same-repo references, where they are already unambiguous.

## Related

- 0016 -- "a citation is a claim about a file, and a file without a commit is not a referent"; this is the same rule for trackers and monikers
- Intent 0054 -- the counter-example: its resolution names devbin a23022f explicitly, and the trace took one command

## Resolutions

**CLOSED 2026-08-24 (vc).** hv adopted the qualification convention the day the issue was filed: cross-estate references are written `<project>#NNNN` for issues and `<project>/<node>` for monikers; unqualified stays legal for same-repo references. Devbin's `usage-rules.md` carries the line (Git section, same commit as this close). Each estate's vc adds its own line in its own tree -- Lamplight's was staged at filing time -- and the upstream Intent guidance candidate rides the round's synthesis via lamplight-vc. The evidence trace (eight repos, each refutation measured, no owner found) stays in this issue's Summary as the reason the rule exists.

**Amendment, 2026-08-24 (same day):** the qualified form is LOWERCASE by definition -- `devbin#0020`, `lamplight/vc` -- matching config-declared project names and session monikers, not the writer's casing. Ruled at the hub after the convention's first hour produced a case split (one estate wrote `Devbin#0020`); raised by laksa/vc, amended fleet-wide so the next estate does not re-split.
